title: who composes a *_latest.json face when the writer only opens a dated file?

population_source.population_definition: every call whose folded destination basename ends '_latest.json', grouped by that basename

call_rule.copy: shutil.copyfile/copy/copy2/move and os.replace/rename carry the destination as the SECOND positional argument
call_rule.direct: open/write_text/write_json/dump_json carry the destination as the FIRST positional argument
call_rule.fold: arguments fold through module, same-function and loop-target constants up to 24 hops (E488/E489 folder)
call_rule.why_e489_missed_it: E489's tracer reads first arguments only, so a copy call looks like no producer at all

class_definition.the_latest_copy_is_a_copy_call_inside_th: one copy call, destination and source fold into the same directory
class_definition.the_latest_copy_is_a_copy_call_out_of_th: one copy call, destination and source fold into different directories
class_definition.the_latest_copy_is_written_directly: one direct write to the latest name
class_definition.the_latest_copy_has_several_static_compo: two or more static composers within the scanned sources
class_definition.no_static_composer_is_found: no composer folds to this name (out of static reach)

method_limits: static only: the population is calls whose destination string folds; a name built from argv/env/a dict key is invisible here and is not counted as absent
a glob-driven copier (e.g. a loop over dated files) folds to the directory, not to the copied basenames, so those faces are published as no-static-composer rather than as copies
scan_directories is declared; a producer living outside scripts/Tools/firm is out of population, not proven missing
C_COPY_SAME_DIR says the two folded paths share a directory; it does not claim the run executed or that the file exists
